rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate: chunk 6 line 52, 'The loop that started with a failing test closed.' 'The loop' is never named earlier inside this file, but per the module-include-order clause the enclosing module's own signposting counts as prior deck-order context: `getting-going.md` line 16 under '## What You'll Learn' (which precedes '## Start here' at line 36, where this exercise is included at line 48) reads '**Run** an orient → fix → close → compound loop end-to-end on a trivial bug in your own repo' — re-verified live this run (`grep -n` against the current file, not carried from any cache). That bullet is the resolving antecedent and sits before this exercise in deck order. Chunk 1/3's 'the bug you fixed' (L13), 'the failing test' (L52) and chunk 3's 'the PR' (expanded prompt) resolve under the session-artifact carve-out (both are the carve-out's own named examples). Chunk 4's 'it' (L43) is immediate continuation of chunk 3's close-out subject. Chunk 5's 'the next agent' (L48) is generic future-session phrasing, maintainer-attested at L119 as Antti's own working frame. No never-named or vague-with-full-history referent found; harm this rule guards against (a slide the reader can't follow because its referent has no antecedent) is not present.

Only external pointer in the body: chunk 3 L35, '[MCP and connectors](../trainings/agentic-engineering-101/reference/mcp-and-connectors.md)', named by its own title in the same sentence ('Adding a connector is one command per tracker'), satisfying the navigational-pointer carve-out.
